fire_nation_war_is_over_royalists_accept.title: Fire Nation war is over: Royalists accept final Salvationist surrender at Suiko; armistice takes effect
fire_nation_war_is_over_royalists_accept.html:
CALDERA CITY, Aug. 12 — Fire Lord Zuko addressed the Fire Nation by radio broadcast yesterday evening, confirming that Royalist forces had accepted the formal surrender of the last Salvationist holdouts in the Suiko industrial district earlier that afternoon. The civil war that began the day the Hundred Year War ended — and that has in some respects never been separate from it — is over. 'We have come through the fire,' the Fire Lord said in a broadcast that lasted eleven minutes.

'Not the fire of glory — the other kind. The kind that does not make you stronger. The kind that only leaves you with a choice about what to do with what remains.'

The broadcast was heard by an estimated 40 million people across the Fire Nation home islands and diaspora communities. This correspondent listened in the press room of the Caldera City Post, where the senior editor — a woman who has covered Fire Nation politics for thirty years — sat quietly through the broadcast and then left the room without comment. The armistice terms were confirmed simultaneously by the Fire Nation Ministry of Public Affairs and the Qianchan Foreign Ministry, which has been the armistice’s primary international guarantor.

The terms are classified in full but officials from both governments confirmed the broad provisions: the Salvationist movement is formally dissolved as a political organization; its remaining military formations are to disarm within sixty days; its leadership — those who survived — will face a civil accountability process rather than military tribunals.

“The fire that does not make you stronger. The kind that only leaves you with a choice.” The decision to use civilian accountability rather than military tribunals for the Salvationists is already drawing criticism from the Loyalist families' associations — those who lost relatives to Salvationist violence during the conflict’s middle years.

A statement from the Association of Families of the 78th Brigade, whose regiment was destroyed by Salvationist forces at the Battle of Jinsha Pass in 107 AG, called the decision 'an insult to the dead.' The Fire Lord’s office has not responded to the statement. Officials close to the armistice process told this correspondent that the civilian accountability decision was the most contested provision in the negotiations, and that the alternative — military tribunals that would have required the Royalist government to try soldiers who had been fighting for what they believed was a legitimate revolutionary cause — was assessed as likely to produce martyrs rather than accountability.

suiko_the_last_battle_three_days_in_an_i.title: Suiko, the last battle: three days in an industrial district
suiko_the_last_battle_three_days_in_an_i.html:
SUIKO DISTRICT, Aug. 13 — The Salvationist movement’s last significant military force was the 'People’s Iron Column' — approximately 2,200 fighters who had retreated into the Suiko industrial district after the collapse of the Salvationist command structure at Jinhou in June. They held Suiko for forty-seven days. The district’s steel foundries and manufacturing plants provided natural fortification and the industrial workers who had been their primary constituency since the movement’s founding provided some continued local support.

The Royalist forces' commander at Suiko, Brigadier Sato Junichi, chose containment over direct assault. 'We had enough bodies,' he told this correspondent. 'What we did not have enough of was reasons to add more.'

The containment strategy held the Iron Column in place while supply lines were cut and the political situation outside the district made clear that no relief was coming. The Iron Column’s commander, a woman known in Salvationist circles as 'Red Crane' — her formal name is withheld pending the accountability process — emerged under a white flag on the morning of August 11. She carried a handwritten note addressed to Brigadier Sato.

The note read, in its entirety: 'We have run out of the things that make continuing possible. We request terms.' Sato replied with a written response granting her the civilian accountability process rather than summary judgment.

The Iron Column laid down its arms that afternoon. 'Red Crane' was photographed walking out of the Suiko gate. She is approximately forty-five years old.

She had been fighting since she was twenty-seven. The photograph shows a woman who looks considerably older than forty-five. It will be published in tomorrow’s edition.

what_the_intervention_at_soka_bay_decide.title: What the intervention at Soka Bay decided
what_the_intervention_at_soka_bay_decide.html:
The Battle of Soka Bay in 109 AG is where the civil war was decided, nine years before it ended. This is not a controversial assessment among military historians — the Loyalist main force was broken at Soka Bay and never reconstituted. Republic City marked the end of the Fire Nation civil war with celebrations that ranged from organized street gatherings in the Earthen Quarter to a more subdued civic ceremony outside the Council Hall, where Council President Raimi spoke for six minutes without once using the word 'victory.' the_war_behind_the_war_eighteen_years_an.title: The war behind the war: eighteen years, and what the Royalist victory means
the_war_behind_the_war_eighteen_years_an.html:
The Fire Nation civil war began on the same day the Hundred Year War ended. This is not coincidence. The war that the world fought for a century produced, within the Fire Nation itself, a set of unresolved questions that Ozai’s defeat made simultaneously urgent and unmanageable: what was the empire, what had it done, who was responsible, and what should come after it. Three factions gave three answers. The Royalists, under Zuko, said: a reformed constitutional monarchy, accountability through process, change at the pace the institution can sustain. The Loyalists, under Azula’s leadership until the Loyalist defeat at Soka Bay in 109 AG and her death in the Duel of the Palace in May, said: the empire was correct, its methods were not mistakes but virtues, what failed was the commitment. The Salvationists said: reform is insufficient, the institution itself is the disease, revolutionary transformation is the only honest response to what the empire was. The Royalists won. This is the correct outcome from this newspaper’s perspective. The Fire Nation required a government that could function, that could implement the Caldera Accords, that could begin the accountability process the TRC requires. Zuko’s government has done these things imperfectly and in progress. The alternatives — a Loyalist restoration or a Salvationist revolutionary state — would have produced outcomes worse for every party including the Fire Nation’s own people. This newspaper says the Royalists won correctly while recording what the victory cost.

The cost

Royalist forces: 84,000 dead, 210,000 wounded. Loyalist forces: an estimated 110,000 dead (records incomplete, because the Kanbukyoku personnel absorbed into the Loyalist coalition were not systematically counted). Salvationist forces: an estimated 67,000 dead. Civilian casualties from the urban phases: 44,000 confirmed, with estimates to 90,000. That is between 305,000 and 461,000 dead in combat and in the urban phases. The Fire Nation’s own estimate, which includes famine, disease and reprisals, is about 3.5 million.

The compromise that made the Royalist victory possible

In 106 AG, the Royalist government preserved the Ministry of National Enlightenment under a new name rather than dissolving it. The Ministry’s broadcast infrastructure and curriculum delivery network were necessary for governance. The reform government did not have the capacity to replace them. The Ministry survived. This is a factual matter, not an accusation. The Fire Lord made a pragmatic decision in a war for survival. The Republican Daily supported the decision at the time and supports it now. We also note it clearly, because the Ministry of Public Information and Cultural Affairs — which is what the Ministry of National Enlightenment is now called — employs former personnel of the Kanbukyoku’s propaganda division, and those people are now in the business of shaping what the Fire Nation believes about itself. This is worth knowing.

“The right side does not mean without compromise. It means the compromises were worth the outcome.”

What the Salvationist movement got right

This may surprise readers of this newspaper, which has consistently opposed the Salvationist faction’s methods and goals. We are stating it plainly because the historical record requires it. The Salvationists correctly identified that the Hundred Year War was produced by a structural arrangement — bender supremacy institutionalized as political order — that the Royalist reform program does not fully address. Zuko’s Fire Nation is better than Ozai’s Fire Nation. It remains a state in which bending ability shapes access to power, social standing, and economic opportunity. The Royalist victory has not changed this. It has made it more acceptable. The Salvationists' analysis was correct. Their methods were catastrophic. These two things are compatible. An accurate diagnosis of a problem does not license any method of treatment. The methods they chose — armed revolution, the specific violence of the Jinsha Pass battle, the Suiko district’s forty-seven-day holdout that cost lives on both sides — produced their own injuries and did not produce the transformation they promised. The ideas survive the faction’s defeat. They will resurface. This newspaper expects to be covering them for the rest of its operational life.

i_was_at_soka_bay_i_think_about_it.title: I was at Soka Bay. I think about it.
i_was_at_soka_bay_i_think_about_it.html:
Liang Jiao, 34, works as a construction contractor in Republic City’s port district. He came here after his discharge from the Qianchan military in 112 AG. He agreed to speak on record.

His account has been lightly edited for length.

On joining the 2nd Expeditionary Division

'I was twenty-five when we crossed into Fire Nation territory. I had done mandatory service, served three years, was released, went back to my family’s construction business in Gaoling. Then the Congress voted 287 to 194 and we got call-up notices.

I thought about not going. I had a life. My father needed me.

I went. I think most of us went because the mandatory service culture means you go when called, even when you’re past the initial service window. That’s what the compact is.

On Soka Bay

'Eleven days. The Loyalist force we engaged was well-organized. Better than I expected from a faction that had been losing for nine years.

The Kanbukyoku training culture produces a specific kind of discipline — they fight well because they were taught to function toward a goal under pressure and they don’t stop easily. We broke them on the eighth day. The last three days were the cleanup, which is the worst part.

Cleanup is when you see who specifically is dead. 'I lost four people from my unit. I know their names.

I think about Soka Bay regularly. Not constantly, but regularly. I don’t think that will stop.

The veterans' support network here in the port district helps. There are more of us than you’d expect.

On what the intervention was for

'I think we did the right thing. I believed that then and I believe it now. The Royalist government is a real reform government and it would not exist without Soka Bay.

But I want to be clear about something that sometimes gets lost in the 'right thing' framing: 847 people from my division died for that outcome. They are not abstractions. They had families.

They had mandatory service obligations that put them in that field. The outcome was worth the cost. The cost was also real.

I want both of those sentences to be heard.

On living in the republic

'Republic City is good. The port district is mostly Fire Nation-heritage and EK-heritage people who have figured out how to be neighbors. We argue about the TRC.

We argue about who owns what. We have the same arguments every week in the tavern. Nobody gets hit.

That’s a good neighborhood. 'I have been watching the civil war end from here. I am glad it’s over.

I am glad the right side won. I am going to have a drink tonight with my neighbors, including the ones whose families were on the other side of Soka Bay, and we are going to not talk about that and talk about something else, because that is also how you live with what happened.'

what_comes_after_the_salvationist_ideas_.title: What comes after: the Salvationist ideas outlive the Salvationist faction
what_comes_after_the_salvationist_ideas_.html:
The Salvationist movement is formally dissolved. Its military formations are disarming. Its leadership faces the accountability process.

By every formal measure it has lost. Its ideas have not lost, because ideas do not dissolve with the organizations that hold them. The Salvationist argument — that the Hundred Year War was produced by bender supremacy as a structural political arrangement, and that structural problems require structural solutions, not reformed monarchies — will persist in Fire Nation political culture as a critique from the left of whatever the Royalist government produces.

It will also persist internationally. This newspaper has been told by sources within the Qianchan academic community that the Gaoling Political Science faculty has received three manuscript submissions in the past year that draw explicitly on Salvationist analytical frameworks while explicitly rejecting Salvationist methods. The manuscripts are not from Salvationist survivors.

They are from Qianchan academics who found the analysis useful. The ideas are moving. They will arrive somewhere.

This is worth watching.

senate_to_debate_nuclear_framework_in_se.title: Assembly to debate nuclear framework in September
senate_to_debate_nuclear_framework_in_se.html:
The URN National Assembly’s Foreign Affairs Committee has scheduled a September session to address the Arms Control Treaty framework established at the First Treaty of Gaoling in 100 AG and revised at the Caldera Accords. The session will consider two questions: whether the current Tieshan provisions adequately reflect the post-civil-war strategic situation, and whether the URN should seek formal observer status in the treaty framework currently managed by Qianchan and the Fire Nation. The URN is not a signatory to the Arms Control Treaty.

The republic’s position since 104 AG has been that as a non-nuclear state it has no treaty obligations and therefore no treaty standing. Assembly member Kira Baolin of the Earthen Quarter delegation has been the primary advocate for observer status, arguing that a republic whose founding territory sits between two nuclear-capable states has a direct interest in the treaty’s terms regardless of its signatory status. The Qianchan Foreign Ministry declined to comment on whether it would support URN observer status.

The Fire Nation’s new government has not issued a formal position. The treaty framework debate is expected to be contentious.

land_commission_s_year_two_report_due_ne.title: Land Commission's Year Two report due next week; early numbers are concerning
land_commission_s_year_two_report_due_ne.html:
The Land Restitution Commission will deliver its second-year progress report to Congress next Wednesday. Sources familiar with the report’s contents told this newspaper the numbers are below the target set in the Commission’s founding charter. Year One target: 25% of contested claims resolved.

Year One actual: 18%. Year Two target: additional 20%. Year Two preliminary: approximately 12-14% additional resolution, pending final certification.

The primary source of below-target performance is the same as in Year One: contested claims involving land currently held by Fire Nation settler-heritage families with pre-Accord legal documentation. The Commission’s authority to override property law documentation is limited by the constitutional framework under which it was established. The claims that remain unresolved are disproportionately the ones where the legal documentation is strongest on the current holder’s side and the historical injustice is clearest on the claimant’s side.

Commissioner Dao Linfang is expected to request an expansion of the Commission’s legal authority in the Year Two report. The request will require Congressional action. The Civic party bloc has previously opposed authority expansion.

The Coalition bloc has the votes to pass it with one or two Civic defections.

port_authority_approves_third_phase_of_h.title: Port Authority approves third phase of harbor expansion
port_authority_approves_third_phase_of_h.html:
The Republic City Port Authority voted 7-2 yesterday to approve the third phase of the harbor expansion project. The approved phase adds twelve deep-water berths capable of accommodating the new generation of heavy transport vessels and includes a dedicated Fire Nation shipping lane — a provision that was the most contested element of the vote. The dedicated Fire Nation lane was opposed by the two Coalition representatives on the Authority board on the grounds that it creates preferential infrastructure for what remains, in practice, a primarily Fire Nation-heritage commercial network.

The Civic majority argued that Fire Nation-heritage shippers represent 34% of the port’s traffic and that infrastructure that serves 34% of traffic is reasonable allocation rather than preference. Construction is expected to begin in spring 119 AG and complete within three years. The expansion is projected to increase port throughput by 40% and generate approximately 800 permanent jobs in the port district, with an additional 2,000 construction positions during the build phase.

the_wrong_victory.title: The wrong victory
the_wrong_victory.html:
The Republican Daily has declared the Royalist victory correct. I want to offer a different framing, not because I preferred the Loyalists — I did not — but because I think 'correct' is doing too much work in that sentence. The Royalist government is better than the alternatives.

This is true. It is also the minimum standard for correctness: being better than two factions, one of which wanted to restore an empire that killed a hundred thousand people in this republic’s founding decade and one of which wanted to burn down the institutional structure before building something to replace it. Being better than those options is not a high bar.

What the Royalist victory preserves, alongside the genuine reforms, is a Fire Nation in which the apparatus that ran the board — the documented, named, recorded Kanbukyoku files — has been disbanded as an organization and its personnel dispersed into other roles. Twelve people have been convicted. Fourteen thousand names are in the Commission’s record.

These numbers are in relationship with each other and the relationship is a problem. I am not saying Zuko should have done otherwise. I am saying 'correct' should be able to contain the full weight of what it means, including the gap between twelve and fourteen thousand.

If it cannot, we should use a different word.

Yun Dashan is a contributing columnist. His views are his own.

first_concord_forum_ends_31_hours_late_w.title: First Concord forum ends 31 hours late with a charter, one Earth delegation that would not sign and no agreement on what a leftist is
first_concord_forum_ends_31_hours_late_w.html:
The first full forum of the Concord of Nations, a body that has existed on paper since the Caldera Accord of 121 AG, closed at 2:10 a.m. on Sunday, 31 hours after it was due to end, with a standing charter signed by 19 of the 23 delegations that came to Caldera City, an Earth State delegation that would not sign, a warning from an exiled king and no agreement on what the word "leftist" means.

Official statement. Palace Protocol Office, Sept. 17, 176 AG (printed in full): "The Protocol Office regrets the delay to the closing session. The Office confirms that the charter was signed in accordance with the rules of the forum. Questions of seating were settled by the delegations themselves."

Why the forum met

The forum was called by Tajisaki and Qianchan after the last forces of the People's Republic of Earth were defeated this year, to give the Concord a standing charter and a standing body of states that would work against the Equalist and leftist movements. It opened on Sept. 14 at the Palace, with Fire Lord Izumi in the chair. Foreign Minister Hayato Mori said it would be "a place where states argue before they arm."

One chair, two claims

One delegation arrived from the Earth lands, and it was led by the Generalissimo herself. Kuvira, who has ruled the Earth State from Ba Sing Se since the coup of 174 AG, came to Caldera City with her spokesman, Chen Yulan, and demanded the chair marked "Earth Kingdom."

The claim was contested before the first session ended. On the second day the United Republic's delegation handed the Protocol Office a letter from King Wu, who has lived in exile in Republic City since 171 AG. It was read into the record. "A general who broke her oath to me asks you for my chair," the letter said. "Seat her, and you will have taught her that a coup is a credential. I ask you only to remember what she did with it."

The Protocol Office placed one chair at the end of the hall with no placard. The Earth seat was left vacant in the charter, and the Earth State's delegation did not sign. Asked by reporters whether her state meant to take a grander name, Kuvira said: "The Earth State will be called what its people call it." Qianchan, which is working with the Royalists to restore King Wu or the old confederation, did not comment on the letter.

What is a leftist?

The disagreement that cost the forum most of its extra day was over Article 4, which commits members to exchange information on groups seeking to overthrow a member's order by force. The United Republic wanted the article to name the Equalists, whom it declared terrorists in 170 AG. Tajisaki wanted "leftist movements" added. The Northern Water Tribe's envoy, Sedna, objected that the term would cover the labor guilds of the north.

The first vote failed, 12 to 8 with 3 abstentions, short of the 14 needed. The article passed on Saturday evening, 19 to 0 with 4 abstentions, after the word "leftist" was struck. Qianchan's Deputy Foreign Minister Shen Lihua abstained. "We came to build a table," she said, "not to agree on who sits at the other side of it."

Interpreters and names

The session was suspended for two hours and forty minutes on Friday when the three court interpreters for old Earth Kingdom speech refused to translate for the Earth State's delegation. The Protocol Office said they had been "released from their duty." The Earth State's text was later read in the common tongue.

The plenary record, kept by clerks, shows "Tajisaki" used 214 times and "Fire Nation" 38 times, 29 of them by the envoy of the Southern Water Tribe, Naalak.

The gate

A delegation from the Sand Union, the Si Wong coalition, was denied a seat and withdrew on Saturday, with a statement that the forum "meets in a Palace and speaks for no desert." Outside the Palace gate, demonstrators carrying banners for the Equalists and the Collective gathered on all three days. Caldera police said 31 people were detained. The organizers said 54.

The Concord's first assembly is to meet in the spring.

This report draws on the plenary record supplied by the Protocol Office and interviews with eleven delegates. The Scire could not confirm the organizers' count of detentions, and could not confirm that the letter attributed to King Wu was written by him.

navy_gives_the_diet_no_account_of_how_ku.title: Navy gives the Diet no account of how Kuvira died as the Earth lands count their dead
navy_gives_the_diet_no_account_of_how_ku.html:
Three months after the reports of Kuvira’s death at the hands of the Avatar, no government has confirmed them, and the Diet was told on Tuesday that the Navy will not supply an account.

The former Empress of the Earth Empire was reported dead in December 182 AG, in the last weeks of the war with the United Republic, and the Avatar’s office has neither confirmed nor denied it. The Earth lands are still counting the cost of that war, and the Diet was asked on Tuesday to vote 60 million crowns of grain credit for the western provinces.

Official statement. Ministry of Foreign Affairs, March 12, 183 AG (abridged): "The Ministry has no information on the circumstances of the death of the person formerly styled Empress of the Earth Empire that it is able to make public. The Ministry's concern is the people of the Earth lands."

The question

Daichi Mori, a member of the Reform bloc, asked the Minister whether Fire Navy ships or pilots in the western theater had witnessed the death. "The Diet is being asked to feed a country whose last ruler died in circumstances nobody will describe," he said, according to the transcript. "I do not ask for her sake. I ask because a state that cannot say how its ruler died cannot say who rules."

Minister Mori said the Navy had ships and pilots "in the region" and that their reports were "not matters for this chamber."

The credit

The grain credit passed, 211 to 94. Members of the Old Guard bloc voted against it, saying Tajisaki had no duty to the Earth lands. Refugees from the western provinces are said by the Concord's relief agency to number about 400,000. The Scire could not confirm that figure.

This article is based on the Diet transcript of March 12 and a statement from the Ministry. The Scire asked the Ministry of the Navy to describe what its crews saw. It had not replied by the time this article went to press.

agna_qel_a_settlers_dig_in_on_the_northe.title: Agna Qel'a settlers dig in on the northern Earth plains as Tajisaki asks for a line on the map
agna_qel_a_settlers_dig_in_on_the_northe.html:
Twelve settlements built by the Kingdom of Agna Qel'a now stand on the northern plains of the Earth lands, two years after the expedition of 181 AG landed, and the Kingdom of Tajisaki has formally asked for a line on the map.

The settlers are mostly from the North, in prefab houses of ice-board and timber, and they have been given grain by the Northern Chief's office. The plains are claimed by the Grand Council of Ba Sing Se, which has not controlled them since 174 AG, and by two village leagues, which say they never left.

Official statement. Ministry of Foreign Affairs, June 2, 183 AG (abridged): "Tajisaki has no claim on the plains. It asks Agna Qel'a to state in writing the boundaries of the lands it holds, so that no ship or caravan of Tajisaki is taken for a trespasser."

Settlers and villagers

In the largest of the settlements, which its residents call New Tupiq, 900 people have been given plots. "We were told the land was empty," said Aput Kalluk, 41, a net-maker. "We have met the people it was empty of. They bring us salt."

Rapa Sun, a village-league elder at Hanjiang, said the settlers' wells had drained a spring that fed three villages. "They did not ask. Nobody asks anymore."

The Chief's office

Agna Qel'a's office said the settlers were "guests of the Earth people" and that no state had been consulted because "no state exists on those plains to consult."

This report is based on a visit to four settlements and interviews with 31 people. The Scire could not confirm the settlers' number, which the Northern Chief's office put at 6,000 and the village leagues at 15,000.

si_wong_states_sign_earth_union_charter_.title: Si Wong states sign Earth Union charter; Ba Sing Se's Grand Council stays home
si_wong_states_sign_earth_union_charter_.html:
Nine states of the Si Wong Desert and the western rivers signed the charter of the Earth Union at Earth Union City on Saturday, agreeing to common tariffs on oil, a common court and a joint force of 8,000, while the Grand Council of Ba Sing Se declined its invitation.

The Union's seat is the desert trading city on the Si Wong oil road. Its first Speaker, Haddad Roukan, said the Union was "not a throne and not a general, but a table."

Official statement. Ministry of Foreign Affairs, April 20, 184 AG: "Tajisaki has sent an observer to the signing. The observer holds no instructions to recognize any government."

Who signed

The signers include the former Sand Union and the river cities of the west. Omashu sent a delegate but did not sign. The Grand Council of Ba Sing Se, which governs the old kingdom's center, said the Union was "a customs league dressed as a country" and that it would not "sit at a table set by oil merchants."

The oil

Under the charter, oil leaving the Si Wong pays a single Union tariff, which the Union says will fund the court and the force. Caldera's shipping houses said they would study it. "A common tariff is a better price than nine," said Keiji Arai, a professor of economics at Caldera University. "It is also one more thing for somebody to fight over."

This article is based on the signing ceremony and interviews with 17 delegates. The Scire could not confirm the size of the joint force.

union_tariff_lifts_price_of_si_wong_oil_.title: Union tariff lifts price of Si Wong oil in Caldera as Diet argues over a fuel levy
union_tariff_lifts_price_of_si_wong_oil_.html:
The price of diesel at the Caldera harbor is up 14 percent since the spring, shipping houses said on Monday, and the Diet has taken up a proposal to put a levy on fuel to protect the fishing fleets of the south coast.

The increase follows the Earth Union's single tariff on Si Wong oil, which took effect in January. Port authorities said Caldera imported 40 percent of its fuel from the Union last year.

Official statement. Ministry of Trade, Oct. 6, 185 AG (abridged): "The Ministry notes the rise in the price of diesel. It has no proposal to set prices. The Diet will decide whether a levy is warranted."

In the Diet

Daichi Mori, speaking for the Reform bloc, said the levy "would tax the fishermen who can least afford it in order to protect the shipowners who can most." A member of the Old Guard bloc, Ishikawa Reiko of Shu Jing, said the Union's tariff was "a tax laid on us by a country that does not exist."

The levy was sent to committee, 190 to 130.

At the harbor

"We do not ask for a favor," said Takeo Sato, 52, who owns two boats at the south pier. "We ask who sets the price of the thing we burn."

The Scire could not confirm the Ministry's 40 percent figure, which was supplied by the harbor authority.

xinan_dominion_says_desert_oil_fields_ar.title: Xinan Dominion says desert oil fields are under 'illegal occupation' and warns the Earth Union
xinan_dominion_says_desert_oil_fields_ar.html:
The Xinan Dominion said on Tuesday that three oil fields in the Si Wong Desert are under "illegal occupation" by the Earth Union and that it "reserves every lawful remedy."

The statement was read on the Dominion's state radio and reached Caldera City through the Concord's technical staff. It gave no date and no field names.

Official statement. Ministry of Foreign Affairs, May 11, 186 AG: "The Ministry has noted the statement of the Dominion. It has also noted that the Union has not responded."

The fields

The Union says the three fields were developed by its own member states and have never belonged to anyone else. The Dominion's statement said the fields lay "within the historic lands of the Xinan people" and that their wells had been "drilled under the occupier's flag."

Speaker Haddad Roukan said the Union would answer in the Concord. "We will not answer a radio," he said.

What is Xinan?

Little is known in Caldera about the Dominion, whose capital the Concord's staff list as "not confirmed." Its envoy did not attend the Concord's spring assembly. The Navy's western observers declined to comment.

This article is based on the Dominion's broadcast, as transcribed by the Concord, and statements from the Ministry and the Union. The Scire could not confirm the Dominion's claim to the fields.

earth_seat_at_the_concord_vacant_for_a_s.title: Earth seat at the Concord vacant for a second time as Ba Sing Se and the Union both claim it
earth_seat_at_the_concord_vacant_for_a_s.html:
The chair marked "Earth Kingdom" stayed empty at the Concord of Nations on Saturday, as it did in 176 AG, after the Grand Council of Ba Sing Se and the Earth Union each sent a delegation to claim it and each refused to sit while the other did.

The Protocol Office, which had hoped for a compromise, placed no one in it. It was the second time the seat has been left vacant since the charter of 176 AG.

Official statement. Palace Protocol Office, March 28, 187 AG: "The Earth seat remains vacant pending the agreement of the claimants. The Concord's business will proceed."

Two claims

The Grand Council's delegation, led by Councilor Yun Baoshan, said the Council governs the capital and the old kingdom's center and is "the Earth Kingdom's only continuing state." The Union's, led by Speaker Haddad Roukan, said the Council "governs a city and a rumor" and that nine member states, an oil trade and a common court were more than that.

Neither could be seated without the other's walkout. "In 176 AG, there was a chair and two claims, and a letter from the king," said Shen Lihua, Qianchan's Deputy Foreign Minister, who now chairs the Concord's seating committee. "Now there is a chair and two states. We have not progressed, but we have more to argue about."

The Fire Nation's vote

Tajisaki abstained on a motion by the Southern Water Tribe to seat both on half-votes. The motion failed, 11 to 9, with 3 abstentions.

{j} The chair marked "Earth Kingdom" stayed empty at the Concord of Nations on Saturday, as it did in 176 AG, after the Grand Council of Ba Sing Se and the Earth Union each sent a delegation to claim it and each refused to sit while the other did.

The Protocol Office, which had hoped for a compromise, placed no one in it. It was the second time the seat has been left vacant since the charter of 176 AG.

**Official statement.** Palace Protocol Office, March 28, 187 AG: "The Earth seat remains vacant pending the agreement of the claimants. The Concord's business will proceed."

## Two claims

The Grand Council's delegation, led by Councilor Yun Baoshan, said the Council governs the capital and the old kingdom's center and is "the Earth Kingdom's only continuing state." The Union's, led by Speaker Haddad Roukan, said the Council "governs a city and a rumor" and that nine member states, an oil trade and a common court were more than that.

Neither could be seated without the other's walkout. "In 176 AG, there was a chair and two claims, and a letter from the king," said Shen Lihua, Qianchan's Deputy Foreign Minister, who now chairs the Concord's seating committee. "Now there is a chair and two states. We have not progressed, but we have more to argue about."

## The Fire Nation's vote

Tajisaki abstained on a motion by the Southern Water Tribe to seat both on half-votes. The motion failed, 11 to 9, with 3 abstentions.

xinan_dominion_refuses_concord_inspector.title: Xinan Dominion refuses Concord inspectors and Fire Lord Izumi orders the western radar kept on watch
xinan_dominion_refuses_concord_inspector.html:
The Xinan Dominion has refused a request by the Concord's technical staff to inspect its reactors, and Fire Lord Izumi has ordered the radar stations on the western sea kept on continuous watch.

The request was made on Aug. 4 after the Concord's staff observed what its report called "an unexplained draw on the Dominion's power grid." The Dominion replied on Aug. 15, saying it had "nothing to show" and that the Concord had "no standing in a sovereign house."

Official statement. Palace, Aug. 19, 188 AG (abridged): "The Fire Lord has directed the Ministry of the Navy to keep the western radar stations on continuous watch. This is ordinary prudence and is not directed at any named state."

In the Diet

Daichi Mori asked whether the posture was "ordinary prudence or a rehearsal." Minister Mori said the question would be answered "in the proper session."

What the staff saw

The Concord's staff report, which the Scire has read, says the unexplained draw is equal to "a medium city" and began in the spring. The report did not say what the Dominion was using it for.

The Scire could not confirm the report's findings independently. The Ministry of the Navy declined to comment on the radar posture.

fire_navy_logs_record_light_and_surge_ov.title: Fire Navy logs record 'light and surge' over the northern pole; Agna Qel'a calls it atmospheric
fire_navy_logs_record_light_and_surge_ov.html:
Fire Navy observatories on the northern sea logged 37 minutes of unexplained light and magnetic disturbance over the northern pole on the night of Dec. 20, and the Northern Chief's office has called it "an atmospheric event."

The disturbance began at 11:12 p.m., according to the logs, which were supplied by the Ministry of the Navy. Compass needles on two patrol ships turned for the length of it.

Official statement. Office of the Northern Chief, Dec. 21, 189 AG (abridged): "A known and harmless atmospheric event was observed over the pole. There is no cause for concern. The Spirit Oasis was closed for a precaution agreed with our guests."

The Spirit Oasis

Residents of Agna Qel'a said armed men without insignia had cordoned the Spirit Oasis that night, and that the cordon was still in place on Tuesday. The Chief's office said the men were "guests." The Scire could not establish who they were. Several residents called them the "white guard."

The Avatar

Asked whether the Avatar, Korra, had been at the Oasis, the Chief's office said it "did not discuss the Avatar's movements." The Avatar's office in Republic City did not reply.

This report is based on logs from the Ministry of the Navy, interviews with 12 residents of Agna Qel'a, and statements from the Chief's office. The Scire could not confirm the cause of the disturbance.

gz_grain_exchange.html:

The Board’s registrar said the granaries of the river provinces were reported full by the district offices, and that no member had asked to withdraw lots from the floor.

The Millers’ Association asked that payment terms be extended from thirty to forty-five days. The Board said it would hear the request on Monday.

* * *

The session continues until the evening bell.

war_ends_with_kuvira_s_death_and_river_t.title: Empire’s river provinces pass to committees as its radio retracts word of Kuvira’s death
war_ends_with_kuvira_s_death_and_river_t.html:
The war in which Tajisaki has fought beside Qianchan and the Republic of Nations against the Earth Empire since Dec. 25, 180 AG has not ended, but the Empire’s grip on the river provinces has gone, and the river towns it left behind are being run by committees of men and women who give out grain.

The Empire’s radio announced Kuvira’s death on Sept. 4 and withdrew the statement the next day. The Empire’s garrisons in the river provinces have since withdrawn or deserted, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Monday that it "does not recognize any authority in the Earth lands as the successor of the Empire."

Official statement. Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Oct. 1, 182 AG (abridged): "The Kingdom of Tajisaki has taken note of the loss of authority in the river provinces of the Earth Empire. It has no instructions to recognize any committee, council or person as the government of the Earth lands."

The committees

In at least nine river towns, committees have opened grain stores that the Empire had closed. In Qiaotou, where a ferry was bombed in December 180 and 47 people were killed, a committee held a public trial on Sept. 19 of three Imperial officials accused of informing, and two were executed the same day. The Scire could not confirm the number of trials.

"They fed us when the Empire took the grain," said Lan Meirong, 44, a boatman in Qiaotou. "I do not ask them for more than that. I do not ask what happens to the next man who is tried."

In the Diet

Daichi Mori, speaking for the Reform bloc, asked whether the committees were "the same people who ran the First Civil War, in new coats." The Minister said Tajisaki would be "watching, not choosing."

This article is based on interviews with 19 people in four river towns, and a statement from the Ministry. The Scire could not confirm the committees' size or leadership.

imperial_ministry_says_republic_attacked.title: Imperial Ministry says Republic attacked Xilan and Cape Hengshan; the Empire is at war
imperial_ministry_says_republic_attacked.html:
The Imperial Ministry of Defense announced at 9 p.m. yesterday that the Republic of Nations had attacked the naval base at Xilan on Nov. 30 and the air base at Cape Hengshan on Dec. 1, and that the Empire "considers itself at war."

The Times has not been permitted to send a correspondent to Xilan or to Cape Hengshan. It prints the Ministry's account below as the Ministry's, and has no second source for any of it.

Official statement. Imperial Ministry of Defense, Dec. 2, 180 AG (abridged): "The Empire's western coast has been attacked without warning by the Republic of Nations. The Empire will answer. The people are asked to remain calm and to expect no other news than that issued by this Ministry."

What the Ministry says

The Ministry said the Republic's forces had destroyed "military installations on the western coast" and killed "a number of loyal servants of the Empress." It gave no number. The Times asked the Ministry for a casualty figure at 10:15 p.m. and was told that none would be published.

What the Times has not been able to establish

Two foreign newspapers reported that the explosions at Xilan were heard across the bay, and one gave a figure of 800 dead. The Times cannot confirm it. It has no named source for the cause of the explosions at either base. The Ministry did not say whether any aircraft of the Republic were seen over either place.

Under the new Press Order of Dec. 1, newspapers of the Empire may print only communiqués of the Ministry of Information on matters of war. The Order does not say what happens to a paper that prints more.

The Times was filed at 11:40 p.m. It will print the next Ministry communiqué as received.

ministry_says_qianchan_ambushed_an_imper.title: Ministry says Qianchan ambushed an Imperial column at the Zaofu–Omashu border; strikes follow
ministry_says_qianchan_ambushed_an_imper.html:
The Imperial Ministry of Defense said last night that Qianchan's Zaofu Iron Guard had ambushed an Imperial supply column at the Zaofu–Omashu border on Dec. 23, killing 19, and that Imperial aircraft and artillery had "answered" on the eastern coast of Qianchan on Dec. 24 and at the border on Dec. 25.

The Times has no named source for the ambush, for the strikes, or for the Ministry's description of them.

Official statement. Imperial Ministry of Defense, Dec. 25, 180 AG (abridged): "The Republic of Qianchan has joined the aggression of the Republic of Nations. Its Iron Guard has killed soldiers of the Empire on the Empire's own road. The Empire's reply is lawful and proportionate."

What is known

The Times has confirmed from a named customs official in Huamu that the Imperial garrisons at the border were reinforced on Dec. 22, a day before the ambush. The official declined to say why.

The Times has not been able to confirm that the Iron Guard, which fields Tiejia-III armor, was at the border on Dec. 23. The Government of Qianchan has not responded to a request for comment.

Press

The Press Order of Dec. 1 remains in force. This report was filed from Ba Sing Se and was submitted to the Ministry of Information before printing, as the Order requires.

The Times could not send a correspondent to the border or to the eastern coast of Qianchan.

bombs_fall_on_the_western_ports_for_a_se.title: Bombs fall on the western ports for a second day; the Empire says it will "answer" the Republic
bombs_fall_on_the_western_ports_for_a_se.html:
Imperial aircraft bombed the western ports of Hanyuan and Dongpu for a second day yesterday, and guns across the gulf shelled the quays, in the heaviest attack on the Republic since the founding.

The Ministry of Defense said at least 600 people had been killed by last evening. Hospitals in Hanyuan said they had counted 410 dead in their wards and the streets around them. The Daily could not reconcile the two figures.

Official statement. Ministry of Defense, Dec. 3, 180 AG (abridged): "The Republic has been attacked without a declaration. Its air defense on the western coast is thin. It is being strengthened tonight."

The sky

The Republic has few interceptors on the western coast. Pilots at Hanyuan said the Imperial aircraft flew in three waves at about 8,000 meters and could not be reached. "We saw them. We could not touch them," said Lan Qiu, 29, who flies a fighter based at Hanyuan.

The Empire's account

The Empire said on Dec. 2 that the Republic had attacked its bases at Xilan and Cape Hengshan on Nov. 30 and Dec. 1. The Ministry of Defense of the Republic said it had no forces within 200 kilometers of either place and had given no such order. "We did not do this," said the Minister. "Someone did, and wants us to have done it."

Congress

The Congress is to meet at noon tomorrow. The President has asked both chambers to sit in joint session.

This article is based on figures supplied by the Ministry of Defense and by Hanyuan hospitals, and on interviews with 11 people in the two ports. The Daily could not confirm the Empire's account of the attacks on its bases.

congress_declares_war_on_the_earth_empir.title: Congress declares war on the Earth Empire
congress_declares_war_on_the_earth_empir.html:
The Congress of the United Republic of Nations declared war on the Earth Empire at 4:10 p.m. yesterday, after a third day of bombing and shelling of the western coast.

The House of Representatives voted 244 to 41. The High Council voted by more than the two-thirds the Charter requires. The vote followed a joint session called by the President.

Official statement. Office of the President, Dec. 4, 180 AG (abridged): "The Republic did not choose this war. It will fight it. Every citizen who has completed national service is a member of the militia of the Republic, and the militia is called."

The debate

Members from the western regions asked for aircraft and air defense, not speeches. "I do not want a declaration. I want fighters over Hanyuan," said Pei Anshan, 51, a Representative from the western coast.

Four members of the High Council voted for the declaration and spoke in favor of it at length. A House member said afterward that the debate had been "unusually short for a vote of such weight." The Daily could not confirm how many members had asked to speak.

The militia

The Ministry of National Service said 1.2 million citizens in active reserve status had been called, under Article 52. The Daily could not confirm that figure.

This article is based on the Congress's record of the vote and interviews with nine members.

defector_names_republic_officers_who_han.title: Defector names Republic officers who handled the false flags; Joint Inquiry opens
defector_names_republic_officers_who_han.html:
An Imperial intelligence officer who crossed the lines last month has given the Republic's Ministry of Internal Affairs records naming Republic officers who handled the incidents of the war's first months, and the Congress voted Tuesday to open a Joint Inquiry.

The Ministry said the records name "a number of persons in the armed forces and in the civil service." It did not say how many. It said it would not name them "until the Inquiry has heard them."

Official statement. Ministry of Internal Affairs, Oct. 8, 181 AG (abridged): "The Ministry has received material from a source in the Empire's intelligence service. The material is being authenticated. It indicates that some of the incidents of Dec. 180 to March 181 were not what they appeared to be."

The Inquiry

The Joint Inquiry into the Penetration of the Republic's Institutions will be made up of members of both chambers. Its chair will be chosen by lot. "It must not be a body that can be led," said a member of the House.

Which incidents

The Ministry said the material concerns the bombing of the Qiaotou ferry, the shooting at Mohe, and the shelling of the hospital ship Gongping at Port Hanyuan. The Daily asked whether it concerned the attack on the Tianhe road convoy. The Ministry said it "could not say."

The Daily could not see the records, or confirm the identity of the officer.

inquiry_names_four_high_councillors_and_.title: Inquiry names four High Councillors and a quarter of the House as agents of the Empire
inquiry_names_four_high_councillors_and_.html:
The Joint Inquiry said Friday that four members of the High Council and about a quarter of the House of Representatives, roughly 75 of 300 members, were working for the Earth Empire, and that the Empire's records show agents in the army staff, in supply and in the shipyards.

The records are those of the Empire's intelligence service, seized in the autumn, when committees overran Imperial offices in the river provinces. They add to the material the defector brought last year.

Official statement. Joint Inquiry, Nov. 20, 182 AG (abridged): "The Inquiry finds that the incidents of Dec. 180 to March 181 were in part arranged by officers and members of the Republic acting for the Empire, and in part by agents of the Empire. The Inquiry will publish the names after each person has been heard."

What the Congress cannot do

With four seats of the High Council tainted, the Council cannot raise the two-thirds it needs to ratify a treaty, to confirm a minister, or to try an impeachment. A quarter of the House is under inquiry. "The Charter we wrote needs majorities that we no longer have," said the Speaker of the House.

The Mobilization Act

The Inquiry said the members who pressed hardest for the Mobilization Act of March 181 were among those named. It said the Act itself had been "steered, not forced."

The Daily has not seen the names. The numbers are the Inquiry's.

congress_passes_the_second_constitutiona.html:
The Congress voted last night to dissolve itself under the Second Constitutional Reform Act, called "the Restoration" in the corridors, which returns the Republic to one chamber, the National Assembly, and adds a Constitutional Court and a vetting commission.

The Act passed the House 190 to 22, with 70 members not voting, and the High Council by the two-thirds required, with the four named Councillors absent. It must be confirmed by referendum.

Official statement. Office of the President, Dec. 15, 182 AG (abridged): "The Republic has learned what two chambers can be made to do. It will have one, and it will have it checked."

What changes

The six Founding Seats of the High Council become six designated blocs inside the Assembly: Fire, Earth, Water, Air and two Non-Bender. The Speaker will rotate yearly among the blocs. The Assembly impeaches, and the new Constitutional Court tries. A vetting commission will check members of the Assembly, ministers and senior officers.

What stays

The Presidency stays, with a Federal Cabinet whose ministers the Assembly confirms. Rights, the right to bear arms and national service are unchanged and cannot be amended.

"We took the Council's six seats and the Reform's president and left the rest," said a member of the House who voted for the Act. "I would not call it elegant."

This article is based on the Congress's record of the vote and interviews with 14 members.

tajisaki_declares_war_on_the_earth_empir.title: Tajisaki declares war on the Earth Empire after strikes on Qianchan
tajisaki_declares_war_on_the_earth_empir.html:
Tajisaki declared war on the Earth Empire at 6 p.m. yesterday, hours after Qianchan did, and the Diet voted its support, 391 to 38.

Fire Lord Izumi addressed a joint sitting of both Houses. "The Empire has struck our ally's coast and our ally's border, and it has lied about why," she said, according to the transcript. "We do not enter this war to be a province's conqueror. We enter it so that the Empire cannot be."

Official statement. Palace, Dec. 25, 180 AG (printed in full): "The Kingdom of Tajisaki is at war with the Earth Empire. The Fire Lord has directed the Ministry of the Navy and the Ministry of War to act with the forces of Qianchan and the Republic of Nations."

The Diet

Foreign Minister Hayato Mori said Tajisaki had been asked by Qianchan to join, and had been in contact with the Republic of Nations since Dec. 3. Daichi Mori, speaking for the Reform bloc, voted yes and asked for "a plain account of what the Fire Navy can do against aircraft that fly above its guns." The Minister said the question would be answered in closed session.

Ishikawa Reiko of Shu Jing, for the Old Guard bloc, said Tajisaki's quarrel was with the Empire's government, not with the Earth lands. "We should say so loudly," she said.

The Concord

The Concord of Nations did not meet. A staff officer said no member had asked for an emergency session, "because one side's members would be sitting on both."

This report is based on the Diet transcript and a statement from the Palace. The Scire could not confirm the size of the forces to be sent.

empire_still_holds_the_sky_over_the_gulf.title: Empire still holds the sky over the gulf; Navy says it lost 31 aircraft in the first 3 weeks
empire_still_holds_the_sky_over_the_gulf.html:
The Empire still controls the sky over the gulf and the western coast, the Ministry of the Navy told the Diet on Tuesday, and the Fire Navy has lost 31 aircraft and two ships in three weeks of fighting.

The Ministry said the Imperial air arm had a bomber that flies higher and faster than anything Tajisaki can send against it. The Concord's technical staff call it the B70. The Ministry confirmed the name and nothing else.

Official statement. Ministry of the Navy, Jan. 14, 181 AG (abridged): "The Navy's carrier groups have contested the gulf. The Navy has lost aircraft and two ships. The Navy has not lost the sea."

The second weapon

Daichi Mori asked about "a weapon of the Empire's that the newspapers of Qianchan call the CL1201." The Minister said it was "a matter for the closed session." Mr. Mori said the Diet had a right to know "what we are fighting." The Speaker ruled the question out of order.

What the Navy wants

The Ministry has asked the Diet for funds for 200 interceptors and for a radar line along the western sea. The Diet is to vote Friday.

The Scire asked the Ministry for the range of the B70. It had not replied by the time this article went to press.

republic_s_congress_dissolves_itself_pal.title: Republic’s Congress dissolves itself; Palace says it "will deal with whoever the Republic names"
republic_s_congress_dissolves_itself_pal.html:
The Palace said on Tuesday that Tajisaki "will deal with whoever the Republic names" after its Congress voted to dissolve itself, and that the Restoration "is the Republic's own business."

Foreign Minister Hayato Mori said the Ministry had been told in 181 AG that the false flags of the war's first months were not all the Empire's work. "We did not know how many hands had been in our ally's house," he said. "Now we know."

Official statement. Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Dec. 16, 182 AG (abridged): "The Kingdom of Tajisaki notes the Second Constitutional Reform Act of the Republic of Nations. It has no comment on the form of another state's constitution."

The Diet

Ishikawa Reiko asked whether Tajisaki's own officers were safe. "A state that cannot say who in its government is loyal has no business lecturing a republic that has just counted," she said, according to the transcript. The Minister said the Ministry of Internal Affairs "has no reason to open such an inquiry."

This report draws on the Diet transcript and a statement from the Ministry.

qianchan_at_war_143_dead_on_the_east_coa.title: Qianchan at war: 143 dead on the east coast, 31 at the Zaofu border, 8 ports shut
qianchan_at_war_143_dead_on_the_east_coa.html:
The Federal Defense Office counted 143 dead on the east coast of Qianchan and 31 at the Zaofu–Omashu border after the Empire's strikes on Dec. 24 and 25, and said 8 eastern ports had been closed to civilian shipping.

Qianchan declared war on the Earth Empire at noon on Dec. 25, by 198 votes to 14 in the House of Representatives and 21 to 3 in the Senate, the Federal Defense Office said.

Figures. Federal Defense Office, Dec. 26, 180 AG: east coast dead, 143; border dead, 31; injured, 612; ports closed, 8; aircraft lost, 17. The Office noted that these figures are from the first day and "will rise."

The east coast

Imperial aircraft struck port installations and radar stations on Dec. 24. The Office said it had no warning of the raid. "The first the east coast knew of the war was the sirens," said Mei Fang, 38, a harbor clerk at Tongyuan.

The Zaofu border

The Zaofu Iron Guard held the pass at the Zaofu–Omashu border on Dec. 25. Suyin Beifong's office said it had "never been at the place where the Empire says its column was ambushed." The Qianchan Report could not confirm either account.

The numbers that are not known

The Defense Office did not say how many aircraft the Empire had committed. It did not say how many of the 17 aircraft lost were shot down.

This article is based on figures supplied by the Federal Defense Office and interviews with 12 people. The Qianchan Report could not confirm the figures independently.

the_air_war_turns_loss_ratio_falls_from_.title: The air war turns: loss ratio falls from 5 to 1 to 1.4 to 1 in four weeks
the_air_war_turns_loss_ratio_falls_from_.html:
The Empire's advantage in the air has fallen from five aircraft lost to the allies for each one of its own on Dec. 26 to 1.4 to one on Jan. 29, the Federal Defense Office said, as Qianchan's and Tajisaki's interceptors have come into service.

Figures. Federal Defense Office, Jan. 30, 181 AG: Allied aircraft lost since Dec. 24, 212. Imperial aircraft lost, 148. Loss ratio in the last week, 1.4 to 1. Interceptors delivered to the western gulf, 96.

What changed

Qianchan's interceptors, sent from the east coast, were joined on Jan. 11 by 60 from Tajisaki. The Defense Office said the allies had gained "a working radar line" on the 18th, which it said had cut the Empire's surprise in half.

The bomber and the weapon

The Empire's B70 bomber still flies. The Office said it had shot down two. It did not describe the weapon the newspapers call the CL1201, and said it would not. "We will not name what we cannot yet counter," said the Office's spokesman.

What has not moved

The ground lines have not moved. The Empire has made three probing attacks, at the Zaofu pass, at the south gate of the desert and on the north-east lowlands, and each has been thrown back. The Qianchan Report asked whether the Federal Council or the House had been told of the CL1201. It had not been given an answer.

The Qianchan Report could not confirm the loss figures.

night_of_no_sirens_empire_s_aircraft_str.title: Night of No Sirens: Empire’s aircraft strike Caldera City; Navy says gulf squadron sunk
night_of_no_sirens_empire_s_aircraft_str.html:
Aircraft of the Earth Empire bombed Caldera City in the dark early yesterday and sank the Fire Navy's gulf squadron at dawn, and no siren sounded until the first bombs had fallen, the Ministry of the Navy said.

The Ministry said four cruisers and nine destroyers were lost, with about 3,100 sailors. The city's Office of Public Safety counted about 640 civilians dead at the naval yards, the arsenal and the rail junction. The Palace district was not struck.

Official statement. Ministry of the Navy, Feb. 3, 181 AG (abridged): "The Empire's aircraft were not detected by the western radar line. They did not come from the west or the sea."

What the city saw

"There was a sound like tearing cloth very high up, and then the yards were burning," said Haruka Endo, 44, a ferry pilot. Observers on the hills saw no lights on the aircraft.

The fleet

The squadron had sailed to cover the yards. It was struck at anchor off Cape Ryujin and again under way. "We fired at the sound," said a gunnery officer who was picked up from the water. "There was nothing to fire at."

Where from

The Ministry said it believed the aircraft had flown from the Si Wong Desert, and that a caravan guide had reported "a shape on the sand the size of a harbor" on Jan. 30. It would not say more.

The Scire could not confirm the Ministry's casualty figures. It was not able to reach the yards.

Cruise missiles fired by high-flying Imperial bombers struck Republic City early yesterday, hitting the Ministry of Defense, the Mint and the western rail yards, and killing about 410 people, the Office of the President said.

The base is a dry-lake strip and a ring of buried hangars. The Office said the airships found fuel dumps, a reactor service bay and cradles for three B70 bombers, and the ruts of "a very large aircraft."

The Office said the search began after the strike on Gaoling on March 4. The Foundation's airships flew over the western Si Wong 63 times. Suyin Beifong's office said an airship pilot had seen "the shadow of the hangar roofs at noon."

What is not known

The Office would not say whether the CL1201 had been seen leaving. It said no allied radar had tracked it.

The war that began on Dec. 2, 180 AG ended today, with the Earth Empire's Xinan command and the three allied governments signing a ceasefire arranged by the Concord of Nations.

The ceasefire took effect on Dec. 24. The Xinan command signed it because the Empire’s army had mutinied and its western coast and north had risen in the first weeks of December, and said it had "no more weapons of that kind ready." The allies said they did not believe it.

Official statement. Concord of Nations, Dec. 31, 182 AG (abridged): "The war is over. The Concord will inventory the Empire's arms. The Concord has not been able to account for the aircraft the Empire calls the CL1201."

The toll

The allies counted about 1.1 million dead on their side, most of them at Yu Dao, Zaofu, Gaoling and Republic City. The Xinan command said the Empire had lost about 120,000. All figures are provisional.

The Scire could not confirm the casualty figures.

council_votes_4_2_to_replace_itself_with.title: Council votes 4–2 to replace itself with an elected presidency
council_votes_4_2_to_replace_itself_with.html:
The Republic Council voted 4 to 2 today to replace itself with an elected President and a two-chamber Congress, ending the six-seat executive that has governed the republic since its founding.

The Speaker of the National Assembly announced the result. Councillors Ujo, Ilama, Zi and Viku voted for the reform proposed by Assembly member Raiko. Council President Tarrlok and Councillor Tenzin voted against. The Supreme Court had found the reform constitutional after several months of review.

What changes

The reform creates a directly elected President on the Qianchan model, but without Qianchan’s states. A transition period will follow, and a referendum will confirm the text. The six councillors signed it on Air Temple Island this afternoon.

The two votes against

Mr. Tenzin said he voted on principle, against concentrating power in one office. Mr. Tarrlok’s office said the reform ends the Council he was elected to lead. In the Assembly debate, the firebender Zoltan, leader of the opposition, called Mr. Raiko a liar and a would-be dictator. Mr. Raiko replied that the republic needed change, that the Equalist threat was "a problem solved by dialogue" and by wider representation, and challenged Mr. Zoltan to a presidential election.

Mr. Zoltan was offered a right of reply and had not responded when this edition went to press.

bombs_hit_pro_bending_arena_on_match_day.title: Bombs hit Pro-Bending Arena on match day; 31 dead, about 104 hurt
bombs_hit_pro_bending_arena_on_match_day.html:
Two explosions wrecked the Pro-Bending Arena in Republic City this morning, killing 31 people and injuring about 104, Chief Lin Beifong of the Metropolitan Police said at 2 p.m.

The first device went off at about 8:47 a.m. on the VIP level, on a match day, and a second followed. Chief Beifong said both were on that level. The tournament has been suspended.

The count

Radio bulletins first gave 19 dead and then 43, and one newspaper ran "Dozens feared dead." The police said they treated the radio figures as unreliable from the start. The 31 and 104 are the Chief’s figures, given at 2 p.m., and the Daily has not been able to check them against hospital records.

What is not known

No group has claimed the attack and the police have named no suspect. Chief Beifong said the investigation would not be rushed to fit a theory. Republic City General Hospital asked the families of the missing to call its desk, and the arena’s management said it would release a statement tomorrow.

This report is based on the Chief’s briefing, radio logs and the accounts of four people who left by the maintenance exit.

assembly_authorizes_martial_law_in_three.title: Assembly authorizes martial law in three eastern zones with 81 percent
assembly_authorizes_martial_law_in_three.html:
The National Assembly authorized martial law in the eastern districts, the Fujishihoro highland zone and the Hengdong agricultural belt this morning, with 81 percent of the vote, four days after the bombing of the Yu Dao police station.

The Assembly met at 9:03 a.m. before three foreign missions. Council President Tarrlok moved the authorization, with a 72-hour review. The order was signed at 10:47, orders went out at 11:00 and troops were in the eastern districts by noon.

The debate

Councillor Ilama, of Yu Dao, called the attacks an act of war. Mr. Zoltan asked for full authorization with no review. Mr. Raiko supported the motion "with oversight." "Security without restraint is not security; it is instability in another form," he said.

Councillor Tenzin was the only councillor to vote against. He cited what his father had written about republics that turned their armies on their citizens. The Assembly members from Hengdong, Longshore, Shicheng and Jianyu voted no.

The toll

The Assembly was told that at least 237 people died at Yu Dao, a figure the Council described as provisional. In the same debate Mr. Tarrlok put the deaths across three strikes at 412 in a month, and Mr. Raiko said "over four hundred." The Daily could not reconcile the figures.

This report is based on the verbatim record of the session.

The Assembly met at 9:03 a.m. before three foreign missions. Council President Tarrlok moved the authorization, with a 72-hour review. The order was signed at 10:47, orders went out at 11:00 and troops were in the eastern districts by noon.

## The debate

Councillor Ilama, of Yu Dao, called the attacks an act of war. Mr. Zoltan asked for full authorization with no review. Mr. Raiko supported the motion "with oversight." "Security without restraint is not security; it is instability in another form," he said.

Councillor Tenzin was the only councillor to vote against. He cited what his father had written about republics that turned their armies on their citizens. The Assembly members from Hengdong, Longshore, Shicheng and Jianyu voted no.

## The toll

The Assembly was told that at least 237 people died at Yu Dao, a figure the Council described as provisional. In the same debate Mr. Tarrlok put the deaths across three strikes at 412 in a month, and Mr. Raiko said "over four hundred." The Daily could not reconcile the figures.

who_was_dava.title: Who was Dava
who_was_dava.html:
Dava was 23. She worked nine years at the textile mill on Harbor Approach, in Longshore, four of them on the same line as her friend Fen. This summer the mill ran twelve-hour shifts and more.

The hours

The Daily reviewed the mill’s shift logs for June. They show lines running past twelve hours on eleven days. A coworker, Pei, caught her hand in a conveyor after thirteen hours on her feet and lost two fingers. Pei’s injury report is in the file.

The notice

By the time clock, management posted a notice about "personal responsibility." Fen said Dava read it for a long time. "She said, I’m going to the demonstration on Saturday. You should come."

Jianyu Square

Dava died at the demonstration, on the pharmacy corner of Jianyu Square, shot by Officer Han of the Metropolitan Police. Fen said Dava raised her hands first, "like I’m not doing anything, look." The police said she rushed a line. Officer Han has been suspended and sent out of the city to relatives near Juniper. A photograph and four and a half minutes of footage circulate, and each side reads them as proof.

What the walls say

Her face is painted ten feet high across the eastern districts, with the words "Say her name." Demonstrators chant it. This story is about why she was there. The mill declined to comment on the notice or the logs.

The Daily has reviewed the mill’s shift logs, Pei’s injury report, the posted notice and Fen’s account.

raiko_sworn_in_as_first_president_as_the.title: Raiko sworn in as first President as the Council hands over
raiko_sworn_in_as_first_president_as_the.html:
Raiko took the oath as the first President of the United Republic of Nations in the Assembly chamber this morning, and the Republic Council that governed for 69 years handed over its powers.

The Electoral Commission’s preliminary count gave Mr. Raiko about 58 percent of the votes against Mr. Zoltan’s 33. The Daily has not seen the final certified figures.

The new order

The President is head of state and government and Commander-in-Chief, elected for four years, with at most two terms. He appoints ministers and justices with High Council consent, has a veto Congress can override by two-thirds, and cannot rule by decree or send the armed forces against peaceful protest. The six councillors’ seats continue as the Founding Seats of a High Council, chosen by national vote. A House of Representatives of up to 300 members sits beside it.

The speech

Mr. Raiko said the Council’s corruption, including the scandal over the Water Tribe seat of 169 and 170, "was the reason this reform was needed, not an accident of it." He said the Equalists would be met with "law, representation and, where the law requires it, force."

Mr. Tarrlok did not attend. Mr. Tenzin was present and said he would "watch the powers of this office closely."

Anyone named in this story was offered a right of reply.

republic_sends_expeditionary_force_to_ba.title: Republic sends expeditionary force to Ba Sing Se; President says it will support, not intervene
republic_sends_expeditionary_force_to_ba.html:
The first transports of the Republic’s expeditionary force left the Republic City docks this morning for the Earth Kingdom, bound for the Royalist armies fighting the People’s Republic of Earth.

The Ministry of Defense said the first contingent numbers about 8,000 troops, with supply ships to follow. The Daily could not confirm the figure. Congress voted the funds last week by a wide margin.

The President’s case

President Raiko said the collapse of the Earth Kingdom after the killing of Queen Hou-Ting on 8 June would not stay on the Earth Kingdom’s side of the border. "We will support the Royalists. We will not govern the Earth Kingdom," he said. Mr. Zoltan said the force was late.

The opposition

The Progressives said the Republic was joining a war in which one of the Royalist commanders was fighting under a throne most Earth Kingdom citizens had hated. Their leader asked what the force’s orders were if a Royalist commander turned on his own king. The Ministry said the orders were "to support the lawful government."

The Fire Nation has said it will send medical supplies and old Hundred Year War firearms. Prince Wu, who fled to the Republic after the bombing, was not available for comment.

The Daily has asked the Ministry for the force’s rules of engagement.

students_riot_in_omashu_against_foreign_.title: Students riot in Omashu against foreign troops; Republic says its soldiers held back
students_riot_in_omashu_against_foreign_.html:
Student demonstrations in Omashu turned into riots last night, directed at the foreign troops stationed with the Western Army, including the Republic’s expeditionary force.

The disturbances were the largest civil unrest in the Earth Kingdom since King Kuei’s reign, according to older residents and the city’s own records. The Daily could not obtain casualty figures from a named authority.

The Republic’s position

The Ministry of Defense said the Republic’s soldiers stayed in barracks and none fired. A Ministry spokesman said the force was "there at the Royalists’ request and will leave at their request."

The students

A student at the Omashu university, who gave her name as Lei, said her friends were not for the rebels. "We did not ask for them," she said, meaning the foreign troops. "We would like to fight our own war, if there has to be one." Posters in the district asked who was paying for the Western Army’s supplies.

The Western Army’s commander, King Guan Shikaei, imposed a curfew from 8 p.m.

The Daily’s correspondent in Omashu reported by telephone.

king_shikaei_shot_dead_at_a_military_par.title: King Shikaei shot dead at a military parade in Omashu
king_shikaei_shot_dead_at_a_military_par.html:
Guan Shikaei, the 31-year-old King of Omashu and commander of the Western Army, was shot dead yesterday at a military parade in Omashu.

Omashu police said the gunman was a university student with Equalist ties, who was arrested at the scene. Generalissimo Kuvira’s headquarters in Ba Sing Se said a Fire Nation spy was responsible and that the Eastern Army would take command of the western front. The Fire Nation’s embassy in Republic City called the claim "an invention." The two accounts do not agree and the Daily cannot confirm either.

The Republic’s forces

The Republic’s expeditionary force, which has served with the Western Army since 171, was put on alert. President Raiko’s office said the Republic mourned "a loyal king and an ally," and called for restraint. The Ministry of Defense said it was asking Ba Sing Se what the Eastern Army meant by "take command."

The question

King Shikaei had argued, since the two Royalist armies joined this year, that the monarchy and King Wu’s authority should be kept. Generalissimo Kuvira had argued that she should lead. The Daily’s correspondent in Omashu said the city was quiet last night, and that soldiers stood at every crossing.

This report is based on police statements, the two commands’ communiqués and the Daily’s correspondent.

concord_adopts_charter_19_to_0_republic_.title: Concord adopts charter 19 to 0; Republic’s bid to name the Equalists falls short
concord_adopts_charter_19_to_0_republic_.html:
The first full forum of the Concord of Nations ended in Caldera City today with a standing charter, 19 votes to 0 and 4 abstentions, after a session that ran 31 hours late.

Twenty-three delegations came and nineteen signed. Fire Lord Izumi chaired.

Article 4

The Republic’s delegation, led by Foreign Minister Han Seojun, asked that Article 4, which commits members to exchange information on groups that seek to overthrow a member’s order by force, name the Equalists, whom the Republic declared terrorists in 170. Tajisaki asked that "leftist movements" be added. The word was struck, and the article passed without a name.

"The Republic will take what the charter gives it," Mr. Han said. "It will not pretend the charter names what it does not."

The Earth seat

The Earth State’s delegation, led by Generalissimo Kuvira, demanded the Earth Kingdom’s chair. The forum left it vacant. The Republic’s delegation read into the record a letter from King Wu, written in Republic City, which warned that seating her would teach her "that a coup is a credential." The Sand Union was denied a seat and withdrew.

Ms. Castellan travelled with the Republic’s delegation.

equalists_declare_war_on_the_republic_an.title: Equalists declare war on the Republic and strike Yu Dao and Republic City
equalists_declare_war_on_the_republic_an.html:
The Equalists declared open war on the United Republic of Nations on 12 September and struck Yu Dao and Republic City the same day, the Republic’s economic and political centers.

The attackers hit the exchange district and the harbor works in Yu Dao, and the Congress precinct and two rail terminals in Republic City. Security councils in both cities sealed their districts and ordered garrison units to the streets. A curfew is in force in Republic City.

No count

The Ministry of Public Safety has not released casualty figures, and the Daily has not been able to confirm any from a named authority. Residents of the Yu Dao exchange district described fires that burned through the night.

The response

President Raiko’s office said the Republic would answer "with every means the republic holds." The Equalists’ statement, which was distributed in several nations, said the aim was to "cut the house of trade and the house of rule at the same time." The attacks were part of coordinated bombings in capitals and regional cities abroad on the same day.

The Fire Nation has offered aid. The Concord of Nations will meet in emergency session this week. Both cities were still operating on 14 September, with disruptions.

The Daily’s offices in the Wada district were not affected.

raiko_resigns_before_end_of_second_term_.title: Raiko resigns before end of second term amid reports of contact with Equalists
raiko_resigns_before_end_of_second_term_.html:
President Raiko resigned today, before the end of his second term, after reports that he had been in contact with the Equalists.

His office said he denied wrongdoing and that any contact had been "to talk, as I said in 170 that talking was needed." The Daily has not seen a record of the contacts and cannot confirm them.

The allegations

Congress’s security committee said it had received material alleging contact before and after the Equalists’ declaration of war on 12 September. Mr. Zoltan, the Nationalist Union’s leader, called the reports "the first honest news about the President in seven years." The Progressives called for a full inquiry before judgment.

The succession

The Vice President will act until the election. The Electoral Commission called a special presidential election for 28 November, for a term ending in 182.

Mr. Raiko’s office was offered a right of reply on the allegations and issued the statement above.

Zhu Li was sworn in as President of the United Republic of Nations this morning, three days after winning the special election as an independent.

The Electoral Commission said she led with a majority of the votes cast. The Daily will print the certified figures when they are published.

Who she is

Ms. Zhu Li worked for years as the assistant of the industrialist Varrick, whom she married. She traveled to Republic City with the Avatar in 170 and entered politics as an independent after the Raiko Reform. She has never joined a party.

The speech

"I have no party," she told the Assembly chamber. "I will have to ask for every vote, every time, and I will." She said her first act would be to publish the inquiry into the attacks of 12 September "before anyone asks me to." The Nationalist Union said it would judge her by whether she did.

congress_passes_mobilization_act_after_h.title: Congress passes Mobilization Act after hospital-ship shelling at Port Hanyuan
congress_passes_mobilization_act_after_h.html:
Congress passed the Mobilization Act today, five days after the hospital ship Gongping was shelled in the harbor at Port Hanyuan, killing 31 people.

The House of Representatives voted 262 to 28. The High Council voted by more than the two-thirds the Charter requires. The debate lasted one afternoon, which several members described as short for a vote of this weight.

What it does

The Act places industry, shipping and rail on a war footing, widens the call-up of reserves under Article 52, and directs the ministries to report weekly to the President. The Ministry of Defense said the shell types recovered at Hanyuan were of the Earth Empire’s pattern.

The doubts

Three Representatives asked that the vote wait for the Ministry’s full report on the shelling. The motion failed. A Representative from the western coast, who voted for the Act, said he did so because "the dead are not going to wait for the report."

The Daily could not confirm how many members had asked to speak. This article is based on the Congress’s record of the vote.
